item.title: A collaborative multi-LLM framework with self-reflection iterative prompting for automated essay scoring
item.description: Abstract Although the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) for essay scoring is not a new concept, these models do not grade in the same manner as humans. This discrepancy arises because humans can adapt their grading patterns based on the specific questions they encounter. In contrast, existing research on this topic typically employs a predefined rubric that fails to address the variability in responses effectively. item.title: The evolution of tool use in LLM agents: from single-tool call to multi-tool orchestration
item.description: Tool use enables large language models (LLMs) to access external information, invoke software systems, and act in digital environments beyond what can be solved from model parameters alone. Early research mainly studied whether a model could select and execute a correct single tool call. item.description: Cybersecurity is changing from reactive, human-centered systems to highly autonomous cyber-capable agents (HACCAs) that can operate at machine speed and scale. item.description: STEM interdisciplinary project-based learning (PBL) asks students to knit together knowledge their courses have kept apart, and to do so while absorbing the ordinary friction of group work. item.title: Neuromodulation-inspired gated associative memory networks: Extended memory retrieval and emergent multistability
item.description: Classical autoassociative memory models have been central to understanding emergent computations in recurrent neural circuits across diverse biological contexts. However, they typically neglect neuromodulatory agents that are known to strongly shape memory capacity and stability. item.description: Genomic analyses such as spatial transcriptomics often generate a large number of candidate targets, but prioritizing targets for functional validation requires expertise across multiple domains and verification across diverse biological resources. item.description: Introduction: Alpha-gal syndrome (AGS) is an increasingly recognized immunoglobulin E (IgE)-mediated hypersensitivity disorder to mammalian-derived products that carries serious surgical implications if not considered perioperatively. item.description: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in natural language processing; however, their effectiveness in specialized domains depends on their ability to represent domain-specific terminology, conceptual relations, and contextual knowledge.
